claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with a few questions:

**What is the name of the child or children you're inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand a bit more about your circumstances.

**Are you currently living in the UK, and do you have settled status or are you a British citizen?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm settled here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and living expenses, or does someone else have primary responsibility for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm responsible for Alex. He lives with me and I take care of him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

**Is Alex in full-time education, training, or does he have any other status I should know about (for example, is he in hospital or local authority care)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex has been in hospital for a while now - about 3 months or so. He's been getting treatment there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that. That's an important detail.

**Is Alex still living with you while he's receiving hospital treatment, or is he permanently residing at the hospital during this time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been staying at the hospital during his treatment - not at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that clarification. Before I make my final assessment, let me check the specific rules regarding children in hospital to ensure I give you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. I've reviewed the relevant rules about Child Benefit for children in hospital.

**One more important question: While Alex has been in hospital, have you been regularly spending money on him (for example, for clothes, personal items, or other expenses), or are all his costs covered by the hospital?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have been spending money on him - I buy him clothes, magazines, and his favorite snacks and things like that while he's there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess your eligibility.

Based on the rules for Child Benefit and the specific guidance for children in hospital, I can provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news!** You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why: While the standard rule is that Child Benefit stops after 8 weeks in hospital, there's an important exception. Because you are regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital (for clothes, magazines, snacks, and other items), you can continue to claim Child Benefit for him even though his hospital stay has exceeded the 8-week threshold.

This exception exists to recognise that you're continuing to provide financial support and maintain your responsibility for your son despite him being in hospital.

**Important:** If you haven't already done so, you should inform HMRC that Alex is in hospital so they have the correct information on file. This will help ensure your payments continue without interruption.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
